content.thinking:
I'm planning to write the full scene in a single careful pass to avoid errors, designing a red panda balanced on a mossy stone in a Genshin-inspired style—sizing the stone and the panda's body, posture, and raised paw for a natural balancing pose.

Working out exact coordinates: stone height, panda root joint and hip placement, leg limb chains with bend parameters, and a spine chain for sweeping the body shape along a curve.

Now I'm defining the tail as its own curved chain arcing up and back from the rump, with radius tapering from thick near the base to thin at the tip, plus striped ring bands for coloring.

Now working through the neck and head joint structure, I'm deciding between a chained approach versus creating the head as a separate joint with explicit position and direction, parented to the last neck joint so its bone aims forward correctly.

For the head geometry, I'm planning a wide scaled sphere for the skull with a painted coat pattern, a smaller sphere for the muzzle positioned lower and forward, a dark nose sphere, and a separate "jaw" joint carrying a cream-colored lower jaw ellipsoid while the upper jaw stays part of the head mesh. For the ears, I'm thinking of extruding a rounded triangle outline with rust coloring and white rims to give them some thickness and proper outward orientation.

Going with cream rim outer ear and rust inner ear, thickness layered so it pokes through both sides for a stylized cutesy look, tilting the ears outward slightly. Now moving to the eyes, planning an anime-style eye decal placed on the head surface.

Making the eyes appropriately sized for the Genshin-style look with amber-ish iris color, positioning the decal on the skull surface with mirroring for both sides, and deciding to skip brow and blush effects to keep the rust-colored face clean. I'm also planning facial markings characteristic of a red panda: cream cheek patches using distance-based blobs from cheek center points, plus darker tear-mark streaks running from near the eyes down toward the mouth, computed via paint functions in head-local coordinates.

Now I'm adding cream brow spots and a separate cream muzzle region against a darker rust forehead, using a distance-based helper for the markings. For the body, I'm setting up a rust coat color with countershading toward dark brown on the belly and legs, then wrapping it in a jagged fur-edge cel shader for that stylized zig-zag look, while keeping legs and paws dark brown with small cream claw details on the toes and planning the tail ring pattern next.

Shifting to the environment, I'm shaping a mossy boulder using a lathe profile with an irregular rounded silhouette, kept low-poly and faceted, with smaller accent rocks made from flat-shaded icosahedron spheres. I'm painting the stone's surface by blending mottled green moss on the upper, noise-displaced boundary against a grey mottled stone base below, and now moving on to building leaf-card moss tufts from an SVG shape.

Scattering dozens of small grass-blade cards across the top of the stone, plus a couple of tiny mushrooms with cream-spotted caps nestled at the stone's edge. For the panda itself I'm considering a cute accessory -- a small gold filigree collar with a tassel -- and working out how to sweep a closed ring of points around the neck's midpoint to form the collar loop.

Since the neck is tilted roughly 30 degrees, I'm adjusting the collar's circle into an ellipse so it fits snugly rather than intersecting oddly, then adding a gold bell charm at the front and red tassel cards hanging down, all rigged to the neck joint. I'm also thinking through placing small gold studs evenly along the collar path to give it that ornate filigree look.

Now I'm planning fur ruff cards for the cheeks and tail tips -- flame-shaped tufts in rust and cream tones, scattered outward from the skull based on position, tinted with pale cream colors rather than full paint objects to keep things simple.

I'm scattering more fur flicks along the body spine using the coat color, roughly 120 cards on the upper body, angled backward to suggest flow. Then I'm defining the overall stance geometry -- stone platform height, foot positions, and the spine curve from rump through mid-back to chest to set up the standing panda pose.

Now I'm working out leg joint placement: hip/shoulder roots, knee bend directions (front legs bending back at the elbow, hind legs bending forward at the knee), and segment lengths so the legs sit nearly straight while reaching from body to ground. I'm structuring each limb as a three-joint chain (hip, knee, ankle) with named bones and a "leg" role, feeding into the parent skeleton.

I'm also sorting out side naming conventions (mapping positive x to the left side) and setting world-space root/target coordinates for front and hind legs, then tapering limb thickness along the chain with a small ellipsoid paw at each foot tip.

I'm checking the paw placement so it sits just at the stone's surface, then reworking the stone itself to be wider and elliptical rather than a flat circle, since the panda's feet extend beyond the current radius—adjusting the lathe profile points to widen the top and taper the base accordingly.

I want faceted segments rather than smooth, so I'm setting a lower segment count on the lathe geometry to get that angular rock look. I'm also scattering a few extra pebble shapes made from flattened icosahedrons around the base using the same stone material, and setting up the root joint position for the whole stone structure.

For the skeleton, I'm wiring the parts near the stone region to an explicit bone rather than relying on nearest-joint detection, then defining the root and hips joints with their positions and parent relationship. I'm building the spine as a short chain following a catmull curve through four points, letting it auto-generate the intermediate joint names, and now setting up the body sweep radius with an ellipse profile function.

Writing ellipse profile function...

Then I'm defining the neck as a short chain between the chest and head base, giving it a thick radius so it visually blends into both the body and the head, and setting the head center point.

Now I'm building the head joint hierarchy with the skull as a scaled sphere, followed by the muzzle as a smaller cream-colored sphere offset forward and down.

Adding the dark rounded nose at the muzzle tip, setting up the jaw joint as a child of head with its own cream sphere part for the lower jaw, and keeping the mouth closed at rest.

For the eyes, I'm working out how to decal onto the skull's surface using the `around` and `at` spherical positioning helper to place mirrored eyes at the right azimuth and elevation so they sit naturally on the head.

Now I'm sizing the eyes relative to head width and thinking through the ear extrusion geometry -- figuring out perpendicular x/y basis vectors so the ear's thickness and outward lean come out correctly.

Then I'm shaping the ear outline as a rounded polygon with an inner contour, planning the two-tone coloring: rust-dark fur on the outside rim, lighter cream or white fur on the inside.

Confirming the z-offset points forward correctly so the ear front faces outward, applying the small positional shift. I'll use cel shading for the ear colors with the rust outer tone and cream inner tone, and leave the chest dark with white cheeks matching real red panda markings.

For legs I'm using a darker brown cel shade with sweeps built from three-joint chains for the hip, knee, and ankle, giving rounded caps. For paws I'm scaling spheres and adding small cream claw spikes at the toe tips, working out whether the chain's tip joint resolves correctly for bone attachment given the three named joints.

Naming each leg joint uniquely with front/hind and left/right suffixes so bones don't collide, then placing claw spikes angled forward from the paw front using the tip joint as their bone, and starting to lay out the tail's path points curving upward and backward from the rump, parented to the hips.

I'm checking proportions so the bushy tail tapers with varying radii along its length while clearing the stone edge, keeping overall body height realistic relative to a red panda's actual head-body and tail length ratios.

Adding ring color banding...

I'm adding small decorative touches like a glowing teal flower and tiny floating elemental seed-orbs near the figure, keeping nothing overhanging above it.

Switching to glowing mushroom caps instead of floating orbs, placing a few at the stone's edge with cream stalks and teal glowing caps with white spots, positioned away from the panda's feet.

I also want to add a gold-trimmed amulet collar with a small glowing teal gem and hanging gold tassels for a Genshin-style elemental accent, figuring out placement around the neck where the collar sits.

Realizing the collar position would clip into the chest and head geometry at that neck point, I'm switching to a head accessory instead -- a small flower tucked behind the left ear with a gold clip, using soft petal colors with a gold center, plus a hanging tassel, and working out the exact offset coordinates relative to the head and ear position.

Adjusting petal scale to elongate radially while staying thin along the normal direction, then placing a gold center sphere and working out the tassel frame so it hangs downward from the hit point.

Adding cheek fur tufts now, scattering hit points on the skull surface and filtering by position and normal to place tuft cards with a flow direction based on sign of x.

Then I move on to body fur, scattering cards across the body sweep surface with similar lean, flow, and bend parameters, using a coat-colored fur card and designing a leaf-shaped tuft texture for the look.

For whiskers, I'm placing thin white rod sweeps from the muzzle point outward, a few per side with flat caps, keeping them very thin for a fine, delicate look.

Now I'm adding tail fur flicks with darker orange tufts angled along the tail direction, moss-green blade cards scattered on stones with appropriate density and lean, and considering small flower accents plus panda-style tear marks and a rust-toned forehead patch for extra detail.

I'm sketching the resting pose as balanced on the stone, hind legs spread with tail raised for stability, and tallying part counts to stay under budget before writing the head paint function that defines cream cheek spots, brow markings, and tear-mark segments using distance checks from key facial coordinates.

I'm verifying the tear and brow positions sit correctly against the head ellipsoid's surface math, then double-checking which imports (THREE, builder helpers, curve utilities) are actually needed to avoid unused-import errors.

Now I'm setting up stone and moss paints using mottle-based noise variation, blending them based on surface normal and position so moss appears on upper and lower patches, then finalizing which texture and math helpers to import.

For body coloring I'm using furEdge to create a rust-to-dark gradient for the belly and chest, wrapped in cel shading, while legs get a darker gradient treatment. Now I'm starting the stone lathe profile outline as a typed array of points for the body shape.

Writing lathe mushroom code...

For pebbles I'm using faceted icosahedron geometry with a squashed scale and stone paint. I'm sketching claw details on the paws and setting up a tail sweep part, then defining the eye decals with mirroring for the left side. Now I'm working through the joint hierarchy—root, hips, and a spine chain with appropriate roles—before attaching hind and front legs to specific spine joints and building the body sweep.

Shaping body profile curve...

Adding jaw joint positioning...

I'm adjusting the jaw position lower so the chin shows below the muzzle, keeping the skull bottom aligned, and now planning a thin dark mouth line sweep between the muzzle and jaw.

For the legs, I'm writing a loop over left/right sides to build front limb chains, computing joint positions and bend directions, checking reach distances fall within limb length, and setting up named chain joints parented to the spine.

Writing leg sweep and paw geometry...

Applying this same rust transition to both hind and front limbs, then setting up the joint chains for hips, knees, and ankles with proper naming. Still need to handle tail joints, body fur cards, and ear coloring before locking in the function signatures for direction input.

Now I'm defining the scatter filter for stone surface placement, checking hit points by normal and position to keep decorations on top surfaces away from the panda's feet. I'm placing a flower using skull skin coordinates on the left side, then moving to designing the tassel texture with a gold knot, cord, and fringe strands in SVG.

Still writing SVG code...

I'm considering the card orientation: since the drawing's root edge (v=0) is at the bottom, viewing from downstream with the lean flipped means the card will hang with its root edge appearing on top.

Positioning the flower using a frame derived from the hit point, then finalizing the TypeScript code with proper typing for the skin intersection and center coordinates.

I'm checking the ring and stick function signatures, confirming scale options exist, and setting the metadata with name, description, style, and commit hash. Then I'm planning the hair tuft placement by scattering card frames across the top of the skull, filtering for points where the surface normal points sufficiently upward.

Finalizing the tuft parameters—count, minimum distance, size range, lean angle, flow direction, and rust tint—before writing everything to the file.
